proposal.description: Start-up from S_OFF tests the gated gate-drive enable en instead of the combined converter enable g_en, confusing the output enable with the enable request
proposal.reason: In S_OFF en_from_state is 0 so en is always low, and the FSM never leaves S_OFF: with en_SW and spi_enable high and no fault, ss_active, en and state_out stay at S_OFF instead of starting soft start.

before: if (~g_en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin
after: if (~en | latch_state | OTP | latch_assert | UVLO) begin
proposal.description: The disable test in S_HICCUP uses the gated gate-drive enable en instead of the converter enable g_en, so the cool-down's own gate-drive-off reads as a disable
proposal.reason: en is always low in S_HICCUP, so after a window trip the FSM leaves for S_OFF one clock after entering S_HICCUP, then restarts into S_SS without waiting for hiccup_done: hiccup_active lasts one clock and the cool-down is skipped.

proposal.description: ss_active is decoded as 'ramping with the gate drive on', so the combinational fault gating of en also drops it before the FSM leaves S_SS
proposal.reason: When a hard fault or disable arrives during soft start, ss_active falls on the same clock as en instead of a clock later when the FSM registers S_OFF. The ramp and the soft-start overcurrent window are therefore cleared one clock early.

proposal.description: hiccup_active is decoded as 'cool-down still running', so a hard fault or disable drops it combinationally before the FSM leaves S_HICCUP
proposal.reason: When OTP, UVLO, the latch or a disable arrives during the cool-down, hiccup_active falls on that clock instead of a clock later with the registered move to S_OFF. The hiccup timer and strike counter are therefore released early.
